A technique to reuse samples from the previous gradient-descent iteration at the current iteration by merging reservoirs from current and previous iterations, treating different iterations as different frames.
A recursive inference step to refine noisy primitive positions by updating offsets $\Delta \mu_i$ based on previous estimation $\Delta \mu_{prev}$.
Update rule: $\Delta \mu_i^k = \text{Tanh}(\mathcal{D}_{pos}(\mathbf{f}_i)) \cdot v_{size}$, where $\mathbf{f}_i = \mathcal{F}(\mu_i^{init} + \Delta \mu_i^{k-1})$.

Each iteration involves one forward projection, one adjoint projection, and a small convolutional network pass.

Partially Learned Gradient Descent originates from the field of learned iterative reconstruction for medical imaging and tomography.

It was developed to bridge the gap between model-based iterative reconstruction (which is interpretable but slow/hard to tune) and end-to-end deep learning (which is fast but lacks physical guarantees).
